head: c3e53d2ff55d41b1e5ea2b01f97efaf61a2fd636
mode: read-only static review; no compiler, socket, daemon or network test execution
conclusion: No confirmed functional regression requiring an integration block was found in the five reviewed files. Observation code does not establish timing neutrality or qualify the original deadline regression.

findings.detail: For the existing call sites the non-test macro branch evaluates the original operation exactly once, introduces no closure or deadline evaluation, and preserves question-mark propagation. Direct observer calls and the observer module are cfg(all(test, unix)).
All installed tokens copy one Instant origin; per-thread observations and deadlines use the same origin. Timestamps are user-space observations, not kernel return timestamps.

Each recorder preallocates 512 events and counts overflow; the completed-record buffer retains at most four recorders and counts excess threads. Current use installs one caller plus three server scopes.

ACTIVE RefCell borrows finish before each original operation. The shared finished mutex is used at scope teardown or emission, not hot-path recording; poison is recovered. Current Scope instances are dropped on their installation threads.

Normal flow joins services before dropping the caller scope and emitting. Local declaration order also puts fixture/service cleanup before Capture on early unwind. Emit catches ordinary output panics and emits at most once.

limitations: Unix test builds add TLS accesses, monotonic-clock reads, event writes and installation allocations. Near the existing 200 ms deadline this can perturb timing and may increase flakes; no zero-overhead claim was established.
Completed recorder blocks are printed in teardown order, not global chronological order. Cross-thread analysis must use the shared-origin at_ns fields.

Logs may be incomplete: overflow and excess_threads must be checked. A question-mark operator inside an instrumented expression may leave the original scope before finish; an unmatched begin does not independently prove a blocked operation.
accept_after_deadline denotes a user-space observation after construction of the existing request deadline; it is not a kernel accept timestamp or proof of expiry.

Buffered output occurs after the original work but catch_unwind does not bound blocking stderr time. panicking describes scope teardown, not the final test verdict; the strict assertion runs after explicit emission.
This static review does not substitute for compilation, actual timing measurements, original-environment acceptance, or theorem/security qualification.
